It premiered on October 4, 2025 on NBC and Peacock during the 2025-26 television season, hosted by Puerto Rican singer and rapper Bad Bunny, with musical guest singer/rapper Doja Cat, and set to conclude on May 16, 2026. In the season, the series reached a milestone: airing its 1,000th episode, on January 31, 2026, with host Alexander Skarsgård and musical guest Cardi B. The opening montage from the previous fiftieth anniversary season is retained but does not remain intact. Most notably, all SNL50 anniversary branding is stripped, either replaced by an ordinary SNL mark or stripped completely. In the title card, the flashing tribute of past logos is removed entirely, and a modified color grade is applied to the wordmark. The musical arrangement remains intact. Additionally, show bumpers are recycled from the previous season, but without the anniversary branding. Contents 1 Cast Changes 2 Cast 2.1 Changes 2.2 Repertory Players 2.3 Featured Players 3 Episodes 4 Promos Cast Changes[] On August 22, 2025, prior to the start of the season, creator/executive producer Lorne Michaels confirmed that changes to the cast were guaranteed and that announcements about any changes would be made in the following weeks. Beginning on August 25, a series of departures was announced, starting with Devon Walker (who had been let go from the show after three seasons - since 2022), followed later by featured player Emil Wakim (who was let go after one season), Michael Longfellow (also let go after three seasons - since 2022), Heidi Gardner (who had been let go after eight seasons - since 2017), and Ego Nwodim (who voluntarily left after seven seasons - since 2018).[7][8][9][10][11] On September 2, 2025, five new featured cast members were announced: stand-up comic Tommy Brennan, Upright Citizens Brigade performer and Dropout TV regular Jeremy Culhane, stand-up comic and Kill Tony podcast regular Kam Patterson, social media comedian and actress Veronika Slowikowska, and Ben Marshall, SNL staff writer and member of the comedy trio and former SNL collaborators, Please Don't Destroy.[9] PDD's time on SNL ended after four seasons (2021-2025) as, along with Marshall's promotion, John Higgins departed the show and Martin Herlihy remained as a writer, who still creates pre-taped sketches written and starring him. Michaels also confirmed that James Austin Johnson will return, noting that the show would rely on Johnson's Donald Trump impersonation for the foreseeable future.[10] Despite Gardner, Nwodim, Longfellow, Walker and Wakim's departures, the rest of the entire cast from the previous season returned. Ashley Padilla and Jane Wickline, both of whom were hired for season 50, remained as featured players. This would be the final season for longtime cast member Bowen Yang, (started on the writing staff in 2018, and he had been a cast member on the show since 2019), as he left the show after seven years following the Christmas episode, hosted by his Wicked co-star, Ariana Grande, on December 20, 2025, with musical guest Cher. He is the sixth cast member to leave the show in 2025, following the former cast members listed above.
